A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TD-VCL research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renamed benchmarks and relocated analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments on PermutedMNIST, SplitMNIST, and SplitNotMNIST, including accuracy comparisons, replay-buffer experiments, and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds CIFAR100-10, TinyImageNet-10, and comparisons involving UCL, UCB, and their TD extensions.

M1.justification: The original n-step KL and TD(λ)-VCL objectives remain unchanged. v2 adds TD-UCL and TD-UCB by incorporating the existing TD objective into UCL's adaptive regularization and UCB's uncertainty-dependent learning-rate procedure, providing additional variants without replacing the core method.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on CIFAR100-10 and TinyImageNet-10, substantially extending coverage to richer natural-image classification tasks. The original MNIST/notMNIST tasks remain under the 'Hard' names, with their existing replay restrictions; the multi-head SplitMNIST comparison is also retained.

E2.justification: The original Online MLE, Batch MLE, VCL, and VCL CoreSet comparisons remain. Tables 3 and 8 introduce actual evaluations of UCL and UCB alongside their TD counterparts across the benchmarks, substantially broadening the Bayesian comparison beyond vanilla VCL and its replay variant.

E3.justification: The added image experiments introduce AlexNet architectures with ten heads, no pretrained representations, and benchmark-specific replay rules, including a three-task memory window for TinyImageNet. Appendix G also adds random search with approximately one GPU day per method, while retaining the earlier grid-search description. This makes the reported tuning procedure inconsistent and does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix K adds per-task forgetting and recovery analyses for CIFAR100-10 and TinyImageNet-10, supported by Figures 8 and 9. The existing replay-buffer analysis, single-head versus multi-head comparison, and n/λ/β sensitivity studies are retained, although several move within the document.

E5.justification: The original three benchmarks retain ten-seed reporting. v2 specifies five seeds for the added CIFAR100 and TinyImageNet experiments. Both versions use 95% confidence intervals for plotted error bars and two standard deviations in tables; no increase in runs for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: All original Table 1 numerical entries are retained. Tables 2–3 and 7–8 add extensive benchmark and method results; for example, CIFAR100 at t=10 reports TD(λ)-VCL at 0.71±0.01 versus VCL at 0.66±0.01. Some newly duplicated results conflict: SplitMNIST TD(λ)-VCL at t=5 is 0.66±0.02 in Table 1 but 0.67±0.04 in Tables 3 and 8.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, and derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–E are substantively unchanged. Adding the explicit qt(θ) assignment to Equation 5 is a notation clarification, rather than a new result or proof correction.

C1.justification: The central claims about mitigating compounded posterior-approximation errors and connecting VCL to TD targets remain. v2 modestly broadens the stated empirical contribution to other VCL-based methods and their TD enhancements, beyond v1's emphasis on standard VCL and non-variational baselines.

C2.justification: v1's broad criticism of multi-head classifiers as unrealistic for CL becomes a narrower argument about MNIST/notMNIST benchmark saturation; v2 explicitly accepts multi-head architectures for harder datasets. Appendix K adds positive-transfer interpretations for SplitMNIST and CIFAR100. Section 6 also softens the explicit requirement to retain n posterior copies into a possible memory increase.

D1.justification: Appendices G–J substantially expand implementation and reproducibility information, including CNN configurations, baseline and TD-variant hyperparameter tables, data/replay specifications, and a tuning budget. The code pointer changes from GitHub to an anonymous repository. Conversely, v1's explicit prior variance and initialization discussion are omitted; their removal does not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for UCL, UCB, other Bayesian CL research, and uncertainty-based motivation. The related-work emphasis shifts from likelihood tempering toward compatibility with UCL/UCB, and the Farquhar–Gal evaluation citation is removed. The fundamental positioning between regularization and replay within variational Bayesian CL remains.

P1.justification: The empirical narrative is substantially reorganized: v1's evaluation-standards subsection moves into Appendix I, benchmark descriptions receive Appendix J, and per-task analyses are consolidated in Appendix K. The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental discussion are revised, with an impact statement and conference checklist added.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparison and full-result tables, expands and restructures hyperparameter tables, and adds two per-task figure sets. It relocates existing analyses, removes v1's dataset illustration and duplicate average-accuracy plot, and changes typography and page layout. The underlying results of several relocated figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's MNIST/notMNIST experiments and VCL-centered comparisons by testing Bayesian CNNs on richer image tasks and examining TD extensions of UCL/UCB. Added per-task analyses and implementation tables make generalizability more assessable. Conflicting table entries and random-versus-grid tuning descriptions weaken reporting; Table 8 also contains a final SplitNotMNIST result where TD-UCL slightly underperforms UCL despite the consistent-improvement claim. These issues limit precision, but the broader, directly relevant validation provides a substantial net improvement.
